clue.text: Bird of ill omen at court

definitions.meaning: a small grey warbler whose male has a dark crown
the square of dark cloth a British judge put on before passing a death sentence

explanation.surface: A bird whose appearance in a courtroom spells doom.
explanation.walkthrough: In British courts a judge donned a black cap to pronounce the death sentence, so it was a sign of ill omen at court.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a warbler species; the second is the judge's headgear worn when sentencing a prisoner to hang.

clue.text: Describing a neat product

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a neat product is something made from cowhide

explanation.surface: An adjective for something tidily made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is an old word for cattle (as in neatsfoot oil), not tidy: the product is the hide of oxen.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective meaning made of tanned cowhide describes goods from cattle.

clue.text: Low form place achieved by one behind the lines

definitions.text: Low form place achieved by one behind the lines

parts.words: Low form place achieved by one behind the lines
parts.note: read as a lowly position taken up by a civilian who trails an army behind the front

explanation.surface: A pupil coming low in class, somewhere behind the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' is a British school class, but here 'low form' means a low sort, and 'behind the lines' is the army's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A civilian who trails an army, selling goods or services, keeps to the rear rather than the front.

clue.text: Companionable dragon

parts.note: a fierce older woman paid to accompany a young lady, stern as a dragon

explanation.surface: A friendly fire-breathing monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dragon' is slang for a formidable older woman, the kind who once escorted unmarried girls in society.
explanation.definitionFit: An older woman who accompanies and supervises a young lady in society is a stern escort.

clue.text: A little Italian instrument

definitions.meaning: the small flute pitched an octave above the ordinary one

explanation.surface: A small instrument from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian adjective means small, and the high-pitched small flute takes that name.

clue.text: How to improve a walnut-tree ? Get away with you !

definitions.meaning: the old proverb says a walnut tree, like a dog, is the better for a beating
a brusque order to go away

explanation.surface: A gardening query followed by an exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: An old proverb holds that 'a woman, a dog and a walnut tree, the more you beat them the better they be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrashing a walnut tree was believed to make it fruit, and the same words are slang for clear off.

clue.text: The boy at Broadcasting House

parts.note: a boy's name that is also a short word for a microphone, found in the BBC's headquarters

explanation.surface: A lad working at the BBC.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcasting House is the BBC's London headquarters, where microphones abound; Michael's short form names one.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of Michael is also slang for a microphone, the broadcaster's tool.

clue.text: Some stride haughtily, others crawl through the undergrowth

definitions.meaning: people who walk with stiff proud steps

explanation.surface: Two kinds of walkers: proud strutters and creepers in the bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk stiffly and proudly is one sense of the verb; hunters who creep up on deer through cover are the other.

clue.text: For instance Bishop Berkeley's port is contained in it

indicators.note: the port and the word 'is' are placed within the two letters of 'it', which holds them

parts.note: taken as written
Deal is a port town on the Kent coast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reference to the Irish philosopher bishop and a harbour of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a seaside town in Kent, England. Berkeley, the Irish bishop-philosopher, held that objects exist only as they are perceived, so he is an example of the answer, as 'For instance' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: George Berkeley held that material things exist only as perceptions in the mind, the classic philosophical stance of that school.

clue.text: Victory at hand

definitions.meaning: the frond awarded to a winner as a token of triumph
the inner surface of the hand

explanation.surface: A win is close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm branch was the ancient emblem of triumph, and the same word names the inside of the hand.

clue.text: Top people act strangely way up in Mexico

indicators.note: the three words behave strangely, their letters falling into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Important people behave oddly while travelling north in Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges the letters of TOP PEOPLE ACT. 'way up' describes a lofty peak, not a direction of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: The volcano near Mexico City rises over five thousand metres, so it stands very high above the country.

clue.text: Try chips once for a change, to celebrate the fifth

definitions.note: a purpose phrase standing for a noun, the display put on for the festival

indicators.note: the three words are changed around so their letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A suggestion to eat fried potatoes as a treat for the festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges TRY CHIPS ONCE. 'the fifth' is 5 November, Guy Fawkes Night, celebrated in Britain with bonfires and fireworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Firework displays mark Bonfire Night, the British festival on that November date.

clue.text: Routed a different way round

indicators.note: the word routed is set out in a different way, with its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Traffic sent along an alternative road to get around something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a different way' rearranges ROUTED; the whole clue also describes the answer, a route taken round an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is a longer road taken to get round a blockage, which is exactly what traffic routed differently follows.

clue.text: Scoring 2 R's out of 3

parts.note: the three R's of schooling are reading, writing and arithmetic; someone managing the first two can read and write

explanation.surface: A test result of two out of three.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three R's' is the British phrase for basic education: reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to read and write, without the sums, means passing two of the three basic school skills.

clue.text: Bend over-for a stroke of the pen, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a line drawn in ink

explanation.surface: Someone stoops forward to write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns 'ink line', a stroke of the pen, into a word spelt differently but sounding the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean or tilt forward is to bow or slope, the sense of bending over.

clue.text: Imbued with a natural impulse

definitions.meaning: an old adjective meaning filled or charged with, used before 'with'

explanation.surface: Filled with an innate urge.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means charged or filled; as a noun it names an inborn urge.

clue.text: Ex-non-commissioned types mind the sheep

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the people who do this, a noun

parts.note: ex means former, in the past
ORs, other ranks, are soldiers who are not commissioned officers

explanation.surface: Former sergeants and corporals now look after a flock.
explanation.walkthrough: OR stands for 'other ranks', the British army term for soldiers below officer rank. The clue's 'mind the sheep' is short for 'who mind the sheep'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy are shepherds of a congregation, their flock in church language.

clue.text: In the new world a man is a boy at heart

definitions.note: a place phrase standing for a person of that continent, a noun

indicators.note: the boy is placed in the centre of the other words, at their heart

parts.note: taken as written
Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A grown man in the New World who is a child at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' puts ERIC inside A MAN, after its first two letters. 'In the new world' stands for someone of the New World.
explanation.definitionFit: The New World is the Americas, so someone living there is a citizen of the United States or nearby.

clue.text: Telephone bird ?

parts.note: to ring is to call by telephone
a dove is a bird of the pigeon family

explanation.surface: A bird that makes calls.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the answer is a pigeon, and its name splits into a call and a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The wood pigeon with a neck band is a species of bird.

clue.text: Are they foiled when making boundaries ?

definitions.text: Are they foiled when making boundaries ?

parts.words: Are they foiled when making boundaries ?
parts.note: swordsmen wield foils, and people who put up fences make boundaries

explanation.surface: Asking whether builders of boundaries are thwarted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foiled' looks like 'thwarted', but a foil is a fencing sword; builders of field fences share the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Swordsmen who fight with foils share their name with workers who put up fences.

clue.text: Where to display a cigarette-holder ?

parts.note: read as a place to put on show a box holding cigarettes, which is one to flourish in company

explanation.surface: A question about where to put a smoker's accessory on view.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'cigarette-holder' here is not the long mouthpiece but the box the cigarettes are kept in, one fit for showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass cabinet for displaying items is also a cigarette box carried to show off.

clue.text: The Spanish idea turns up on an ancient Roman bench

definitions.note: a phrase describing the magistrate who sat there, used for the noun

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the words are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish notion appears on a seat in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses EL IDEA as a whole, in a down clue read upwards, giving AEDI + LE.
explanation.definitionFit: This official was a Roman magistrate responsible for buildings and games, sitting in judgement on such matters.

clue.text: Once perhaps in the East, or in the dawn of time

annotationWithheld.why: Once perhaps in the East, or in the dawn of time (6): the anagram of ONCE inside E (East) gives five letters; no clue word supplies the second E the answer needs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Once perhaps in the East, or in the dawn of time

clue.text: Opening bars of "Getting to know you "?

definitions.text: Opening bars of "Getting to know you "?

parts.words: Opening bars of "Getting to know you "?
parts.note: the first bars of the song are its musical prelude, and getting to know someone starts with being presented to them

explanation.surface: Asking how the show tune from The King and I begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting to Know You' is a song from The King and I; its opening bars are the prelude, while meeting someone starts with being presented.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical prelude opens a piece, and being presented is how acquaintance begins.

clue.text: Whittington's act that received an encore ?

definitions.text: Whittington's act that received an encore ?

parts.words: Whittington's act that received an encore ?
parts.note: Dick Whittington was told by the bells to go back again, and a music-hall act is a performer's spot

explanation.surface: A music-hall performance by Dick Whittington that was called back.
explanation.walkthrough: In the English legend Bow Bells rang 'Turn again, Whittington', calling Dick back; a music-hall act is also this word, and 'again' is the encore.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's spot on a variety bill is so called, and Dick Whittington was bidden to do it again.

clue.text: With which one presses on to the green

definitions.text: With which one presses on to the green

parts.words: With which one presses on to the green
parts.note: read both as the hot appliance used to press clothes and the golf club played to reach the putting surface

explanation.surface: A golfer pushing on towards the putting surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presses' is laundry: the appliance smooths clothes, and in golf the same name is given to the club used for an approach shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The household appliance presses cloth flat, and the metal-headed golf club takes a player onto the putting surface.

clue.text: 0, what a letter!

parts.note: the round letter O has that shape, and a letter sent to many people is a mass mailing

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at receiving some mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O' is a letter of the alphabet shaped like a ring, and 'letter' is also a piece of post sent out in bulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaped like a ring describes the letter O; a printed notice sent to many is a mailshot letter of that name.

clue.text: The old-fashioned villain was never right

definitions.meaning: a stage baddie of melodrama looks menacing and evil
in heraldry and Latin the word means on the left side

explanation.surface: A melodrama baddie who was always in the wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word for 'left' gave English its word for ominous, and heraldry still uses it for the left-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil-looking menace marks the melodrama baddie, and the Latin root means left, never on the right hand.
